images.prompt:
Transform this supplied photograph into a carefully constructed MOIRE INTERFERENCE ARTWORK made from TWO OVERLAPPING LINE SCREENS. Make this construction immediately visible; ordinary engraving hatching is not the intended style.

Keep the exact full photograph composition: two separate full-body adults, woman on the left with one arm raised diagonally to the upper center and her other arm lowered left, man on the right with both arms lowered. Keep their recognizable faces, positions, outfits, four hands, four bare feet, the wide space between them, the left window and the floor perspective. Do not crop, duplicate anatomy or merge the people.

Build the image with TWO equally visible independent continuous navy line systems on warm ivory paper. First system: roughly vertical parallel lines about 2 pixels thick, spaced about 12 pixels apart. Second system: lines of the SAME ink darkness and thickness spaced about 13 pixels apart, tilted approximately 12 degrees relative to the first. BOTH line systems MUST actually be drawn throughout the large wall area. They must visibly cross, producing a lattice of long narrow diamond openings. A viewer must be able to trace both independent directions and see real acute-angle intersections. The second system is not a faint texture, shadow, or variation of the first line's thickness.

Gently curve and slowly vary the second system's spacing across broad areas so the real superposition generates large, low-frequency undulating interference waves. Make several distinct slow beat bands conspicuous at normal image size, especially across the upper wall and the large empty space between the figures. The line crossings remain crisp within the dark and light beat bands. Never substitute solid wavy stripes or a single field of wavy lines.

Translate source light and shade through line spacing and overlap density; keep figure-ground contrast, the dark clothing shapes and all body boundaries readable. Within large clothing shapes continue the two-system crossing mechanism with restrained curvature. Leave small identity-critical facial details, hands and toes in quieter fine linework so identity and anatomy stay legible. Use clean matte ink and subtle paper grain, no photographic texture, no random digital glitches, no scan artifacts.

One complete unframed 4:5 image, at least 1024x1280 pixels. No labels, text, borders, watermarks, logos, signatures, symbols, inset examples, split screens, or extra objects. Output only the finished artwork.
